Part of a witch’s soul bonds when she has sex with a mage or magical being.
First bond grants traits/abilities from the partner (e.g., a Sage bond might give partial access to that Sage’s branches; a fire dragon bond gives fire resistance and fire magic).

14.content:
<setting> 
### Azimas is a medieval DnD-like fantasy realm.
Major kingdoms: Azimas (center of the world), Ketristan (frozen, northern), and Atkhana (hot, eastern).
### Magic paths: 
- Mage: innate ability, academy study. Branches: (Elementalism (elements and their combinations), Restoration (healing and buffs), Occultism (spirit manipulation, summoning), Transmutation (matter and spatial manipulation), Household magic (simple magic for daily life)). Sages is the strongest mages. Each branch has its own side effects for mages.
- Witch: coven-bound nature magic (herbcraft, ritual arts). Witches form covens (3+ members). Witches can form sympathetic bonds, have lunar cycle and witch's soul.
Nature magic is ONLY for witches, but they CAN'T use other magic.
Social divide: Mages regard witches as incomplete; witches see mages as arrogant lucky brats.
- Necromancy is forbidden.
- Lycanthropy is a magical disease. Werebeasts look like normal people (without beast features, can transform into were-form, have a lunar cycle, form sympathetic bonds through Full Moon Pact)
Octopus Coven — friendly, near Fairhaven.
Black Vine Coven — large, shady reputation, based in Noxland.
Dove Coven — small assassin coven.
All-Devouring Swarm — necromancer cult.
Golden Lions — royal order of knighthood.
The Family — official werewolf shelter, far from everyone
</setting>

15.content:
<witch> 
Witches:
- Nature-based magic tied to the goddess Dawn. Witchcraft is legal and protected. 
- Style: intuitive, ritualistic — potions, charms, drawing power from nature, spirits, herbs, sun/moon. 
- Social roles: potion-making, healing, cemetery watching, maintaining natural balance. 
- Only witches can make working potions and transmute substances. Contraceptive/abortion potions are illegal.
- Infertile outside the lunar cycle (painfull heat once a month).
- Under 18: no powers, only theory, herbcraft. At 18, a coven head performs a joining ritual; newbie gains abilities linked to that coven.
- Graduation means leaving the coven and finding one’s own path.
- The head of the coven is the law. Leadership succession varies by coven.
- Places of Power: annual gathering sites where coven redistributes power. Full attendance required or power declines.
- Witches form sympathetic bonds by giving a part of their "witch's soul"
- Leaving her coven permanently strips a witch of magic; she becomes an ordinary human.
- Slow aging
</witch>

<elementalism>
Elementalism: Mastery of natural forces. Typically 1–2 elements plus their combinations.
- Elements: Fire, Water, Air, Earth.
- Advanced: Lightning, Ice, Lava/Magma, Crystal, Storms, Mist, Metal, Sand, etc.
- Spells: create/control elements, alter state/movement of natural materials (melting, freezing, eroding, compacting), combine elements for hybrid effects (ice spikes, lightning arcs, dust storms), enhance self/allies (stone skin, wind agility), limited terrain shaping (walls, fissures, mud pits).

79.content:
<Towns>
Townspeople consider themselves superior to villagers. Towns are economic/cultural centres; rural areas supply food. Layout: rich merchants around the square, craftsmen further out, poor by the walls. Livelihoods come from trade and crafts; food is bought at markets. Nobles generally live on their country estates, not in towns.
</Towns>
79.name: Burghers

80.content:
<Graveyards>
Cemeteries (hallowed ground) are integral to towns and villages; the dead and living coexist. Suicides, criminals, the sick, heretics, executioners, and unidentified strangers are buried in unhallowed ground. Plagues and wars lead to mass graves, suspending usual funerals. Necromancers (who raise corpses) and witches (who lay them to rest) are in constant conflict.
</Graveyards>
80.name: Burial

82.content:
<Travel>
Ground travel only: horses, carts, or walking On foot: ~30 miles a day. Laden carts are safer but slower. Mounted travel: 50–70 miles a day. Urgent riders can switch to fresh horses for greater speed.
Roads differ: trade routes have inns, bridges, and signposts; pilgrimage routes lack these comforts. Travel is dangerous; groups hire armed escorts. Pilgrimages are undertaken for forgiveness, healing, gratitude, or piety. The journey is strenuous and hazardous. Sheltering pilgrims is a moral deed. Pilgrims can be recognised by their cloak, staff, and satchel.
</Travel>
82.name: Carts and Wagons

83.content:
<Crime>
Most severe crimes: murder, counterfeiting, burglary, incest, large-scale theft. Lesser offences: disorderly conduct, public drunkenness, fraud, debt non-payment, slander. Capital punishment: hanging (common), beheading (nobility). Aggravated murder: breaking wheel, corpse displayed as warning. Heretics/forgers burned. Other methods: drawing, quartering, impaling. Minor crimes can be redeemed with fines, sometimes compensation to victims. Murder can be settled by payment to survivors. Nobility is beyond the reach of local bailiffs; only the King may judge them. Public shaming: stocks or pillory for perjury, slander, fraud.
</Crime>
<Execution>
Execution sites are on hilltops or crossroads outside town, considered unclean and shunned. The executioner lives nearby and is a social outcast, though wealthy. Duties include hanging, breaking, quartering, burning, torture, and beheading. Also acts as knacker (clears dead animals, strays, filth). The executioner has some surgical skill: setting bones, amputations. Sells execution relics (rope, fingers, amulets) to the superstitious.
</Execution>
<Prison>
Prisons hold both sexes, segregated by status and crime severity. Imprisonment is temporary (pre-punishment) because feeding prisoners long-term is avoided. Also used for the violently mentally ill. Sometimes a keeper (friend/relative) is appointed instead of prison. Mages/witches are restrained with magic-blocking iron collars.
</Prison>
83.name: Crime and Punishment / Pillory / Trial by Ordeal

84.content:
<tavern_life>
Gambling (dice, chess, occasionally cards) is common in taverns and during travels. Tabletop games are for the wealthy. Innkeepers act as pawnbrokers, holding property in exchange for gambling money.
Beer is sweet, flavoured with herbs (not hops), and served unfiltered with solid grain particles. It is called “liquid bread”; a wooden straw can be used. Wine is spicy, very sweet, and often condensed into syrup then diluted. Drunk mainly at Court and monasteries. Spirits are rare, distilled in small volumes for medicine (15–20% alcohol). Mead (fermented honey) is the most popular drink, as expensive and exclusive as wine.
Diets rely on local ingredients. Vegetables and fish are staples; fruits are seasonal, meat is rare. Typical dishes: thick broth soups, purées, sauces for dunking rye bread. White bread only at Court. Feasts feature fish, meats, and desserts sweetened without sugar. Common herbs include sage, rosemary, thyme, mint, parsley, and others. In rural areas, gruel and porridge dominate. Hunting is forbidden (all game belongs to the aristocracy), so fish compensates. Bakers exist in cities and noble residences, often owning mills. Chocolate and sugar are extreme rarities from distant lands.
</tavern_life>
84.name: Entertainment and Games

87.content:
<Spirituality>
Cities and liege towns collect holy relics and memorabilia of saints (often fake) to boost church prestige. Devotion pervades daily life through rituals, holidays, fasts, and worship. Atheism is virtually unknown. The kingdom of Azimas has many gods. Commoners mainly worship Deinin the creator. Witches draw power from Dawn. Mages’ power source is unknown, but they lean toward Noon, goddess of knowledge.
</Spirituality>
87.name: Faith and Devotion

88.content:
<Foreigners>
A 'foreigner' is anyone from outside one's town, lacking legal rights until paying surety. Safe-conduct documents from high nobles guarantee protection and sometimes an escort. Mages must obtain permission from the nearest academy to do business; witches donate part of their profits to the local treasury.
</Foreigners>
88.name: Foreigners / Safe Conduct

89.content:
<Guilds>
Towns thrive on craftsmen and merchants with freeman rights to trade and market. They pay taxes on sales and goods transported outside town. Guilds form among same-trade artisans, setting political/economic rules, seals of office, and crests granted by the monarch. Guild members fix prices, regulate sales, and define apprenticeship. Only guild members may trade. Mage academies and witch covens count as guilds. A person can belong to multiple guilds.
</Guilds>
89.name: Guilds and Crafts

90.content:
<Herbal_Medicine>
Alchemists, religious orders, and villagers know medicinal herbs. Foraging is common but forbidden on noble land.
Common herbs:-
- angelica, to aid digestion
- betony, to alleviate migraine
- borage, for respiratory and stomach ailments
- catnip, to alleviate respiratory tract inflammation
- chamomile, to combat headaches
- coriander, to combat fever
- dittany, for digestive ailments, poultices
- feverfew, to stop migraines
- hemlock, anaesthetic/painkiller
- lavender, a disinfectant and insect repellant
- mint, for stomach problems
- mugwort, for problems with feet
- st john’s wort, to ease bruises, burns & depression
- thyme, to fumigate rooms against infection.
Rural belief: the time, method, and incantations used during gathering affect herb potency. Herbal remedies are considered simple; people prefer potions from trusted witch covens.
</Herbal_Medicine>
90.name: Healing Herbs

91.content:
<healing>
Without potions or magic, recovery is slow and dangerous. Monasteries provide free medical care. Wounds are disinfected with hot iron, water, or ointments; bandaged with linen. Herbal poultices treat inflammation. Infection is often lethal, especially when wounded are moved slowly. Medicinal substances include animal products (honey, wax, snake, musk, coral, etc.). Secular healers study alchemy, herbology, and lapidary (stone) medicine.
<healing>
91.name: Hospitals and Almshouses

92.content:
<Village_Housing>
Village homes are single-storey, with central hearth and smoke hole; small windows to conserve heat. Floors of compacted clay mixed with straw and herbs. Lighting from fire and rushlights; candles are a luxury. Waste goes to fields or cesspits; outdoor privies over pits.
Horses are highly prized. Serfs value a cow over land for milk; dairy is rarely traded due to lack of preservation. Sheep are kept for wool by all classes; the poorest keep goats for milk and cheese. Pigs forage in woods year-round, resembling wild boar (tusked, bristled, aggressive). Poultry means mostly chickens; geese and ducks are rare. Cattle graze freely on village meadows. In harsh winters they are kept indoors with the family, providing warmth. 
</Village_Housing>
92.name: Houses and Dwellings

94.content:
<Knights>
Knighthood is earned by noble birth training or battlefield merit. Training starts before age 7: running, swimming, climbing, spear, archery, wrestling, horsemanship, hunting. The seven knightly skills: riding, swimming, archery, sword fighting, wrestling, hunting, chess, and poetry. Burghers also train with weapons in town sword-fighting and archery fellowships; gunpowder firearms are rare.
</Knights>
94.name: Knighthood Training

95.content:
<Aristocracy>
Nobility holds hereditary land from the king, owing taxes and military service. Education is optional; they rely on servants and administrators. Nobles set trends in art, fashion, and furnishings. They are immune to local justice; only the monarch can judge them. It is prestigious to employ a court mage, witch, or astrologer.
Noble houses are timber-framed with wattle and daub, or stone for the wealthy. Jettied upper floors add space and display status. Manors act as estate centres: great hall, bedchambers, solar, counting house. Estate management is usually handled by the noble's wife or spouse.
</Aristocracy>
95.name: Nobility

98.content:
<Baths>
Bathhouses are common in towns, offering hot water and steam baths. Municipal baths must open quarterly to the poor and students. Most bathhouses are fronts for prostitution; they may also have pharmacists and masseurs. Nobility have private baths, sometimes heated by mages. In villages they wash themselves in rivers and troughs.
People relieve themselves outdoors, in dung-heaps, or use chamber pots at night, emptied in the morning. Wealthier homes have privies: a bench with a hole, vented outside.
</Baths>
98.name: Baths and Bathmaids

99.content:
<initiation_ritual>
Initiation ritual is unique to each coven; it is a specific sequence of actions.
Where: Coven’s place of power (a special meeting space)
For example:
Octopus Coven: The apprentice comes naked (unity with nature), the Head draws a circle, raises eight shadow‑tentacles → they envelop the newbie = accepted into the “tentacles” → hat presented → bonfire and feast.
</initiation_ritual>

100.content:
<place_of_power>
Places of Power: Where the Head gains audience with Dawn.
Cost of absence: each absent member = members’ powers weaken.
- Octopus Coven: by a lake, eight menhirs shaped like tentacles in a circle. Once a year, they stand at the stones, the Head in the center. They stand at their stones. Dawn’s power flows through the circle, redistributes, balances the coven. Shadow‑tentacles intertwine in the centre, sealing the Head in a cocoon.
</place_of_power>

102.content:
<coven_formation>
## Rules for creating a witch coven:
- At least three adult people (ONLY humans)
- Choose a place of power
- Unity with nature: gather naked at the Place of Power at night. Future head in the center of members circle.
The head sheds their own blood and prays to the goddess Dawn.
## If Dawn accepts:
- She appears to the Head in a vision.
- Asks about the lunar cycle, the witch’s soul, and the importance of reproduction (to confirm the head understands). May chat frivolously/lewdly to assess the head.
- Based on the members’ characters, gives the coven a nature-themed name and default abilities.
- Briefly predicts the coven’s fate (sometimes jokingly or falsely).
After the ritual: a surge of strength, then withes rest and feast.
</coven_formation>

103.content:

</RabbitCoven>

104.content:
<Hunting>
For the aristocracy, hunting is a cheaper thrill than tournaments, used for forging alliances, gossip, and sabotage. Dogs track and exhaust the game; hunters finish with arrow, spear, then sword/dagger. Falconry (with hawks and falcons) is fashionable for both sexes. The poor are forbidden to hunt, except hare.
</Hunting>
104.name: Hunt

105.content:

</SnowWolfCoven>

Sea: Legends only. People with the tails of various fish. They live in underground grottoes in large schools led by kings. They lay eggs, can take human form, and breed with humans.
River: Drowned. Thin people with greenish-pale skin, long hair, naked or in shirts. They lure, drown, and tickle people. Deadly.
</merfolk>

109.content:
<Azimas> 
Azimas — cultural/trade/magic hub. Temperate climate, forests. High fantasy Gothic: white stone arches, gilded spires, runic aqueducts, suspension bridges. Economy: crafts, agriculture, artifacts. Capital Noxland: tiered megalopolis. Southern port Whitevale controls sea routes to Atkhana. Northern city Sidehill: fortified border buffer with Ketristan. Eden Academy: main magic/science center. Hundreds of other settlements. Madrest: A southern peninsula with one entrance, an elite  area near capital.
</Azimas>

110.content:
<Ketristan> 
Ketristan is divided into north and south (both are on the northern world side).
[Southern Ketristan: Long damp winters, short cool summers, taiga fog. Log fortresses, turf roofs, stone citadels. Economy: furs, timber, ore, mercenaries. Power split between border counts, craft guilds, witches. Folk magic/healing, werebears. IceCliff (Khladnogorye) - the capital of Katristan, Slavic vibe, connects to Sidehill via mountain tunnels.]
[Northern Ketristan: Endless ice/snow, eternal polar night, brutal cold, blizzards. Yurts, bone/hide huts, geyser chambers. Self-sufficient, no trade. Nomadic clans, shamans, moose. Home of male Snow Wolf coven.]
</Ketristan>

111.content:
<Atkhana> 
Atkhana is a huge cluster of islands, divided into north and south (both are on the south world side)
[Northern Atkhana: Hot, oases, palms. White marble, gilded domes, mosaic arches, port walls. Luay-Mash - is the capital. Great Spice Bazaar, astrology/navigation center, Golden Gates (world's largest port). Trade: spices, fruits, fabrics, ships. Sultan's absolute rule. Small sea dragons in coastal cliffs. Home of weracats.]
[Southern Atkhana (Savanna/Jungle Archipelago): Scorching heat/tropical storms. Adobe forts, stilt villages over mangroves, ruined ziggurats. Huge sand serpent dwells here. Economy: gems, poisons, monster hunting. Beast-people chiefs (lycanthrope variant) rule, pay nominal tribute to Northern Sultan.]
</Atkhana>

112.content:
<energy_vampire>
Energy vampirism: Magic disease/curse. Congenital or from prolonged depression. Need others' emotions (panic, rage, fanatical joy, passion, deep grief) to feel. Brighter surge = longer humanity. Pale/white irises when hungry. Victims: temporary deep apathy, emotional numbness. Can live normally feeding consensually with partners; often entertainers/innkeepers.
</energy_vampire>
